extra.message: User-controlled `term` (from request body, only length-checked by zod) is interpolated directly into a SQL string passed to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(). The single-quoted ILIKE clauses are not escaped, allowing SQL injection (e.g. term = "' OR 1=1 --").

The `formula` query parameter is interpolated into `new Function('context', 'with (context) { return (' + draftFormula + '); }')` and executed server-side. A vendor_manager can supply arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. `basePrice; process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id')`) for remote code execution.

Vendor-controlled `phrasing` is passed to compilePhrasingPattern(), which builds a template literal and evaluates it via `new Function` (lib/templates.ts:43). A vendor_manager can inject `{{...}}` expressions or raw `${...}`/backticks to execute arbitrary code server-side.

A support_agent can start an assist session on ANY user id (including marketplace_admin) and receives a JWT with sub=target.id. The requireAuth middleware re-fetches the user by payload.sub and adopts that user's role, so the support agent can impersonate the target and escalate to admin privileges.

The `template` value (z.string(), not an enum) is interpolated into a shell command string and executed via `spawn(cmd, { shell: true })`. An admin can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `--template=std; rm -rf /`) for command execution.

The `batchTag` route parameter is joined into a filesystem path without sanitization (no path.basename), so a vendor can write files anywhere on disk (e.g. batchTag = '../../../../etc/...') via fs.writeFileSync.
The `fileName` route parameter is joined into a path and read back without sanitization (no path.basename), allowing arbitrary file read via path traversal (e.g. fileName = '../../../../etc/passwd').

loadLetterTemplate() joins the caller-supplied templateName directly into a path with no traversal guard, so a staff caller can read arbitrary .txt files (template = '../../../../etc/...'). Reachable via disputes.ts:239 (GET /api/disputes/:id/letter/:template).

docName is taken from the vendor-controlled storefront layout (returnPolicyDocName) and joined into path.join(policyDocsRoot, docName) with no allowlist (unlike the warranty variant at line 581). A malicious vendor can set it to '../../../../etc/passwd' and cause arbitrary file read for anyone who opens the return-policy packet.

The `x-spec-sheet-source` header is passed directly to fetch() with no URL/host validation (contrast with mirrorVendorCatalogImage at line 639 which uses an allowlist). A vendor_manager can make the server fetch arbitrary internal/cloud-metadata URLs (SSRF).

The `q` query param and the `recentColleagueId` cookie are interpolated directly into an LDAP filter string without escaping (contrast with verifyEscalationApproverGroup at line 312 which uses escapeDirectoryFilter). This allows LDAP filter injection (e.g. q = '*)(objectClass=*' to enumerate the directory).

renderCatalogSharePage() embeds product.title into an inline <script> string literal without JSON/HTML escaping. Since title is only tag-stripped (plainText) and not quote-escaped, a stored title containing a double quote breaks out of the JS string (e.g. `x";alert(document.cookie);//`) yielding stored XSS on the public share page.

cwe: CWE-80: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags

extra.message: The User-Agent header is reflected directly into the HTML footer without HTML escaping (contrast with orders.ts:398 which uses escapeHtml). This is a reflected XSS sink via an attacker-influenced header.

res.redirect(partnerReturnUrl) uses the raw `x-partner-return-url` header with no allowlist/validation (contrast with users.ts:196-200 which restricts to ALLOWED_ACCOUNT_RETURN_PATHS), producing an open redirect.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: A hardcoded fallback payment-gateway shared secret is baked into the source and used by /api/payouts/gateway/clearance-ping (payouts.ts:227) to authenticate settlement pings that mark payouts 'paid'. Any authenticated user who knows this public default can forge clearance pings in any environment where PAYMENT_GATEWAY_SHARED_SECRET is unset.
A hardcoded partner loyalty-feed credential is used as a Bearer token fallback (syncLoyaltyLedger), exposing a live integration secret in source code.

applyStorefrontLayout() merges the raw request body via deepMerge() (lines 6-20), which does not filter __proto__/constructor/prototype keys — unlike safeDeepMerge() used by applyDigestPreferences(). A vendor can send {"__proto__": {...}} to pollute Object.prototype via the storefront layout endpoint (vendors.ts:213).

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes (Prototype Pollution)

extra.message: saveProductDraft() spreads the entire request body into prisma.product.update data. A vendor_manager can set arbitrary fields — including status='published' and moderationState='approved' — bypassing the moderation/admin-approval workflow, or reassign vendorId.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: reapplyDeliveryPreferences() spreads the JSON-parsed deliveryPrefs cookie directly into prisma.order.update data (contrast with the schema-validated reapplyGiftPreferences at line 522). A buyer can forge the cookie to modify arbitrary order fields such as totalCents or status.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: resolveListingPreviewLink() uses jwt.decode() (no signature verification) instead of jwt.verify(). An attacker can forge a token with arbitrary vendorId/productId and read non-public product details (title, description, imagePath, status) of draft/rejected/unpublished listings.

redeliverNotificationDigest() reads the x-digest-attempts header with no upper bound (contrast with redeliverWebhookEvent at line 182 which caps at 5) and loops sendEmail() that many times, allowing an authenticated user to trigger an unbounded number of DB writes (DoS).

When worksheet=expanded, the error handler returns err.message and err.stack to the client. The ledger lookup error message embeds the full URL including the ledger API key (outbox.ts:39-43), leaking the credential and stack traces.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: findPromotionByClaimPattern() compiles the user-supplied claimCode into a RegExp without escaping. A buyer can inject regex syntax (nested quantifiers like (a+)+$) causing ReDoS, or alter matching semantics via the preview endpoint (products.ts:278).

getWholesalePricing() trusts the client-supplied accountType cookie ('wholesale') to grant a 20% discount without any server-side entitlement check (contrast with getEarnedWholesalePricing at line 264 which checks order history). A buyer can set the cookie to obtain wholesale pricing.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
